steps.rationale:
Serves: every landing's wall, and the owner's direction of 2026-11-09 to use native Go testing to improve performance and drop unnecessary tests.

Disappears: repeated setup and duplicate scenario walks where the measurements identify them; the amount of wall time saved remains to be measured. Across the last fifteen landings the invariants stage took 2m21s to 3m18s, internal/landing 140 to 171 s of it, on every landing whatever it changed.

The twenty slowest are all parallel end-to-end landing scenarios at 103 to 201 s of wall each: TestTwoWorktreesLandThroughOneQueue 201 s, TestTrunkCheckoutFollowsWithItsOwnChangesKept 200 s, TestEveryStageFailureLeavesTheTrunkAlone 198 s, TestWorktreeCandidateIsIntegratedOntoTheTrunk 190 s, TestEveryRuleRefusalFixesOrPrintsItsEdit 181 s, and on. The step measures first, by stage of a scenario, where a scenario's time goes: the fixture repository, the tools it builds, the git and go commands it runs. The part every scenario repeats is then built once for the package (a fixture made once and copied per scenario, with Go's own test caching left to work), and scenarios that walk the same landing to different assertions are folded into subtests of one. The check named here holds the shared fixture. If the measurement finds the time elsewhere, the check is reset to what it finds before this step lands.

Retain isolated mutable repositories and each concurrency, failure, recovery and undo assertion, including the distinction between an assertion detecting removed behavior and a compile failure that supplies no undo evidence. Compare package wall and setup executions under equivalent conditions; do not add overlapping parallel test durations or count Go cache hits as new savings.

steps.title: A finished frame is converted on the card to the 8-bit BT.709 YUV 4:2:0 FFmpeg encodes and handed to it as is, so the host reads an eighth of the bytes, keeps no float copy of the frame, and FFmpeg converts nothing
steps.rationale:
Serves: finished clips written faster and in less memory, the effect no longer waiting on the host.

Disappears: four host passes over every finished frame. Today a 3328 x 1920 frame comes back as 77 MB of float32 (finishingEncoder.add: MemcpyDtoH, then a loop rebuilding 19 million float32 values into a second 77 MB slice). The MP4 encoder then converts it value by value through a callback into 19 MB of rgb24, compares it pixel by pixel with bytes.Equal against a 19 MB copy of the frame before, and pipes it to FFmpeg, whose scaler converts it to YUV on the CPU. On rtx-vsr/nvenc's student clip, 81 frames finished at four times, the effect took 3.8 s of a 10.4 s write (7.8 frames a second), so about two thirds of the time is host work. Each stream holds about 197 MB of host buffers.

The fix: the effect already writes 8-bit RGBA on the card. NvCVImage_Transfer converts it there to BT.709 limited-range YUV 4:2:0 (8-bit RGB where the runtime writes no YUV), which is downloaded, 9.6 MB a frame at four times, and piped to FFmpeg as raw yuv420p tagged as clip-encode/colour-709 tags it. The float path stays for unfinished clips. ChangedPixels is counted on the bytes FFmpeg is handed, the change of what it counts named in the record.

Check: TestAFinishedFrameReachesTheEncoderAsEightBitYUV finishes the student clip at four times. The host must read width x height x 3/2 bytes a frame, the decoded frames must be within 40 dB PSNR of the float path's decoded frames, and two writes must be the same bytes. BenchmarkFinishedClipWrite (test-surface/judge-tests) gives frames a second and bytes allocated a frame, before and after, in the landing's message.

Predicted effect: about 16 frames a second at four times (the effect alone runs 21), and about 30 MB of host buffers a stream in place of 197 MB.

Disappears: a loop no run has closed. docs/TRAINING_COMPATIBILITY.md holds 26 training claims, 25 of them real-artifact-smoke (a route executes and moves weights, most over 1 to 12 steps), and MOSS's 400 steps move a loss the MOSS document itself says is narrower than better pictures. Evidence: both reviews of 2026-11-09 name training breadth ahead of its depth as the main gap between what the system is for and what it has shown. The optimizer's one rate rule (P to the -0.6) is held by tests on particular models; a real campaign is its first reading at length, and a run that does not gain is that reading, recorded as a null result with what the detectable gain was.

The model and objective here are the smallest that serve the purpose and are the owner's to change before the run: a person chooses what training starts from. The bar is fixed before the run: gain above the detectable gain on the held-out view, 300 cases or more, one run, no second run for a better result. The device hours are bounded from one measured step before launch.

Predicted effect: held-out-quality of the trained row above its base's by more than its detectable gain, or a recorded null; the base's cells hold.

Evidence limits: 300 cases is a proposed minimum, not a guarantee of power. Fix the detectable effect and uncertainty calculation for independent held-out units before exposure; correlated tokens or questions do not increase the independent sample count. Record an inconclusive or null result without relaxing the bar. Parameter-count learning-rate scaling is a versioned empirical policy for the workloads already measured. If training-side evidence contradicts it, compare a bounded alternative through the existing recipe-bound policy before the held-out judgment; do not tune by repeatedly consulting held-out results or add a second optimizer-policy framework. Keep smoke completion, loss improvement and improved user output as separate claims.

Inception features under-rate diffusion models (Stein et al., arXiv 2306.04675), and DINOv2 is already native in overgo, so FD-DINOv2 costs no download.

steps.title: The RAE and SimpleDiffusion samplers run as one captured CUDA graph with fused norm, activation and RoPE kernels and several images a batch
steps.rationale:
RAE's DiT-DH-XL works on 256 tokens a 256 x 256 image, and SimpleDiffusion runs in 0.85 s at 0.56 GB: both are bound by kernel launches and fixed overhead, not FLOPs, so quantisation would not help them.

steps.title: DPM-Solver++ 2M runs RAE and SimpleDiffusion at 10 to 20 passes, read at equal passes against the 50-step Euler ODE
steps.rationale:
At low pass counts deterministic multistep solvers beat Euler: DPM-Solver++ 2M reaches FID 4.31 at 10 NFE on VP ImageNet-256 (arXiv 2404.14507). The solver comes from k-diffusion (MIT). That evidence is from other models, so it is compared at equal passes on overgo's own reading.

Serves: first-output, held-out-quality.
Disappears: nothing; the reference preset stays.
Evidence: the solver preset's FID and FD-DINOv2 at 10 and 20 passes are recorded beside the 50-step reference.
Batch: device lane.

steps.title: DiTDH-XL with DiTDH-S epoch 20 as its AutoGuidance guide reaches its paper's quality on RAE's reading
steps.rationale:
RAE is served with no guidance. Its served recipe names the DiTDH-S epoch-20 checkpoint (internal/rae/recipes/sampler.json), which is the paper's default AutoGuidance guide; the paper's best result pairs it with DiTDH-XL at scale 1.5: gFID 1.51 to 1.13 at 256 x 256 (arXiv 2510.11690). The paper also finds plain guidance helps RAE only inside an interval, and from step 1 it raises FID. DiTDH-XL is downloaded once its size and licence are read (decision rae-xl-download).

Serves: held-out-quality.
Disappears: nothing; the unguided recipe stays.
Evidence: the guided preset's FID and FD-DINOv2 are recorded beside the unguided recipe's.
